extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators and practitioners who file or defend IPR petitions before the PTAB (PTAB counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the PTAB's exercise of discretion under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) (the Fintiv framework): the six Fintiv factors and surrounding case law about when the Board should deny institution of an IPR in view of parallel district-court (or other forum) proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching standard: efficiency, fairness, and the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fintiv factors "relate to whether efficiency, fairness, and the merits support the exercise of" discretionary denial; the Board takes a "holistic view of whether efficiency and integrity of the system are best served by denying or instituting review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factors overlap and some facts may be relevant to more than one factor; the Board balances all relevant circumstances when deciding whether to exercise discretion under § 314(a). Parties should present facts showing how efficiency, fairness, and the petition's merits tip the balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 1: Whether the court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted if a proceeding is instituted
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the district court litigation is stayed (or likely to be stayed) pending resolution of a PTAB trial. A district court stay "allays concerns about inefficiency and duplication of efforts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A district-court stay has strongly weighed against exercising authority to deny institution. A denial of a motion to stay can sometimes weigh in favor of denial of institution (unless there is reason to think the court will reconsider if PTAB review is instituted). If no stay was requested or granted, this factor is generally neutral. The Board will not speculate about how a district court will rule on a stay absent case-specific evidence (Sand Revolution II; Fintiv II). The factor applies similarly where an ITC trial date exists earlier than a PTAB decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 2: Proximity of the court’s trial date to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for a Final Written Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Examines timing between the district court's scheduled trial and the PTAB's projected Final Written Decision (statutory deadline: not later than 1 year after institution, 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11)). If the court's trial date is earlier than the projected Final Written Decision, that often favors denying institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the trial date is at/about the same time or after the projected PTAB Final Written Decision, the Board will weigh other factors (e.g., investment in parallel proceeding). Panels differ about how to treat uncertainty in trial dates: some take trial schedules at face value absent strong contrary evidence; others give weight to evidence of scheduling uncertainty. The Board may focus on proximity to the final written decision as a proxy for likelihood the court will reach validity issues first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 3: Investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers the amount and type of work already completed in the parallel litigation (by both the court and the parties) at the time of the institution decision. Substantive orders (e.g., preliminary injunctions, detailed claim construction orders) by the district court favor denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board gives weight to substantive progress (detailed Markman orders, injunctions, substantive rulings). A countervailing consideration is petitioner diligence: filing promptly after learning of asserted claims weighs against denial; filing late or contemporaneously with patent-owner responses may weigh for denial. The Board will consider practical burdens (e.g., many patents/claims challenged, multiple petitions filed in short time) and extraordinary circumstances (e.g., office closures) in assessing investment and timing (see Sotera, Samsung). The level of detail in district-court orders matters (two-page Markman order less persuasive than detailed one).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 4: Overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the petition presents the same or substantially the same claims, grounds, arguments, and evidence as are before the district court. Substantial overlap raises concerns of inefficiency and risk of conflicting decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of overlap is highly fact dependent. Petitioners can mitigate duplication/conflict concerns by stipulations (e.g., not pursuing the same grounds in court if PTAB is instituted); broader stipulations (not pursuing any ground raised or that could have been reasonably raised in an IPR under § 102/103 on printed publications/patents) are more persuasive. Panels have accepted broad stipulations as tipping this factor strongly in favor of institution (see Sand Revolution, Sotera).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 5: Whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party
rubrics_metrics.description: Looks to whether the petitioner before the PTAB is also a defendant in the district-court litigation; historically, when the petitioner is the district-court defendant this factor has tended to weigh in favor of denying institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the district court litigation is stayed pending IPR, this factor may be neutral or only slightly favor denial. There are differing views among judges/panels about the appropriate weight—one dissent argued the factor should be neutral when parties are the same (to avoid penalizing petitioners merely for being defendants). Consider this factor in the context of other Fintiv factors (e.g., stay, overlap, investment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 6: Other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Catches additional case-specific circumstances not encompassed by the other five factors, explicitly including the merits of the petition. The Board will consider particular strengths or weaknesses that might tip the balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are encouraged to identify particular strengths or weaknesses of their positions to aid the Board. Typical arguments under this factor have included the presence of parallel petitions, the number of prior challenges/assertions of the patent, and any other relevant circumstances. Panels have treated this factor flexibly and used it to weigh matters that affect overall fairness and system integrity.
